title: PhenoVoxel Archive · 50-specimen surface and posture review
method: Individual same-viewer side/front/top captures and sampled supported behaviors at visible playback times. Static screenshots are diagnostic, not measured biomechanics. Missing features, rendering defects, incomplete behavior and unverified specimen identities are distinct. Photos/micrographs retain imaging/developmental context and external licenses. A single picture is not a universal phenotype or posture standard.

surface: Leaflets have uniform flat green surfaces; no resolved midrib/vein pattern or varied cuticle.
Flower balls and stems are overly regular.
shape: Sparse tiered shoots and repeated leaflet sizes; branch/petiole transitions, bipinnate rachis and pulvini need clearer differentiation.
motion: Touch-response samples show little leaflet closure in side view; inspect hinge axis and leaflet support.
Growth uniformly resizes the mature flowering plant, including its established organs; this is not organ development.

comparison.text: Leaflets fold at tertiary pulvini and petioles can bend at larger pulvini; an overall mature-plant resize does not show either mechanism.
comparison.scope: Qualitative comparison; no measured coordinates, physiology, trajectories or forces imported. Existing species-account/cached literature and new primary/institutional checks are distinguished from specialist validation.
